{{Nihongo|'''Takashi Gojobori'''|五條堀 孝|Gojobori Takashi|born October 24, 1951, [[Fukuoka]]}} is a Japanese molecular biologist who is vice director of the [[National Institute of Genetics]] (NIG) and the [[DNA Data Bank of Japan]] (DDBJ) at NIG in [[Mishima, Shizuoka|Mishima]], Japan. Gojobori is a distinguished professor<ref name=KAUST>{{Cite web|title=Takashi Gojobori|url=https://cemse.kaust.edu.sa/cbrc/people/person/takashi-gojobori|access-date=2023-02-11|website=KAUST Research Portal|language=en}}</ref> at [[King Abdullah University of Science and Technology]] (KAUST) in [[Thuwal]], [[Saudi Arabia]]. He is a professor of bioscience and acting director at the Computational Bioscience Research Center at KAUST.<ref name=KAUST />

He has also been co-appointed as the special research consultant of the [[National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology]] (AIST), and acts as a visiting professor at [[Keio University]], [[University of Tokyo]], and [[Tokyo Institute of Technology]].  

He is an associate member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO), a member of [[Academia Europaea|Academia Europea]] and an academician member of the [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]], Vatican.

==Education==
Gojobori finished his Ph.D. in theoretical population genetics (1979) at [[Kyushu University]], Japan. He was a research associate and research assistant professor at the [[University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston]] (UTHealth) for 4 years (1979–1983). He was also visiting assistant professor at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] (1985, 1986) and visiting research fellow at the [[Imperial Cancer Research Fund]] (ICRF) in London (1989).

==Research==
He is the founding editor of the journal ''Genome Biology and Evolution'', the executive editor of the journal ''[[Gene (journal)|Gene]]'', academic editor of ''[[FEBS Letters]]'', associate editor of ''[[Molecular Biology and Evolution]]'' and ''[[PLOS Genetics]]'', and section editor of computer genomics in ''[[BMC Genomics]]''. He has served on the editorial boards of six international journals including ''[[GigaScience]]''. Previously he was the editor of ''[[Journal of Molecular Evolution]]'' for eight years (1995–2003).{{citation needed|date=April 2015}} He is leader of the Japanese team of the [[H-Invitational]] international consortium who was tasked with creating a database linking the 21,037 validated human genes to their biological function.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/dn4906-bumper-compendium-of-human-genes-released.html|title=Bumper compendium of human genes released|author=Carrington, Damian|author2=Cohen, Philip|date=2004-04-20|work=[[New Scientist]]|access-date=2019-05-28}}</ref>

Gojobori has worked extensively on the rates of synonymous and non-[[synonymous substitutions]], [[positive selection]], [[horizontal gene transfer]], [[viral evolution]], [[genome evolution]], and comparative [[gene expression]]. In recent years, he has focused on the evolution of the brain and [[central nervous system]],<ref>{{cite journal|author=Gaudet, P.|display-authors=et al|title=Towards BioDBcore: A community-defined information specification for biological databases|doi=10.1093/database/baq027|journal=Database|volume=2011|article-number=baq027|year=2011|pmid=21205783|pmc=3017395}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|pmid=3444411|year=1986|author1=Nei, M.|title=Simple methods for estimating the numbers of synonymous and nonsynonymous nucleotide substitutions|journal=Molecular Biology and Evolution|volume=3|issue=5|pages=418–26|author2=Gojobori, T.|doi=10.1093/oxfordjournals.molbev.a040410|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|pmid=16141072|year=2005|author=Carninci, P.|title=The transcriptional landscape of the mammalian genome|journal=Science|volume=309|issue=5740|pages=1559–63|display-authors=et al|doi=10.1126/science.1112014|bibcode=2005Sci...309.1559F|s2cid=8712839}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Mammalian Gene Collection Program Team|display-authors=et al|doi=10.1073/pnas.242603899|title=Generation and initial analysis of more than 15,000 full-length human and mouse cDNA sequences|journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]]|volume=99|issue=26|pages=16899–16903|pmc=139241|year=2002|pmid=12477932|bibcode=2002PNAS...9916899M|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Okazaki, Y.|display-authors=et al|doi=10.1038/nature01266|title=Analysis of the mouse transcriptome based on functional annotation of 60,770 full-length cDNAs|journal=Nature|volume=420|issue=6915|pages=563–573|year=2002|pmid=12466851|bibcode=2002Natur.420..563O|doi-access=free|hdl=10161/11223|hdl-access=free}}</ref> and [[COVID-19]] or virus transmissions.

Gojobori has served as the Program Director of the Council for Science and Technology Policy (CSTP) of the Government of Japan and is the Science Officer of the Ministry of Education, Science, Sports, Culture, and Technology (MEXT). He has contributed to databases such as DDBJ/GenBank/EMBL and the [[H-Invitational]] human gene database.<ref name=TWAS>{{Cite web|title=Gojobori, Takashi|url=https://twas.org/directory/gojobori-takashi|access-date=2021-08-18|website=TWAS|language=en}}</ref>

He has had more than 400 publications in peer-reviewed international journals on comparative and evolutionary genomics.<ref name=TWAS/> Gojobori has also contributed to the [[GenBank]] database construction as well as the H-Invitational human gene database.

==Honors==
Gojobori is a Foreign Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (2006) and fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS) (2005).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/sites/default/files/AnnualReports/2005/2005_2225_Fellows.pdf|title=2005 AAAS Fellows|access-date=2019-05-28}}</ref> In 2006 [[Pope Benedict XVI]] appointed Gojobori as a member of the [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.casinapioiv.va/content/accademia/en/magisterium/benedictxvi.html|title=Benedict XVI|publisher=Pontifical Academy of Sciences|access-date=2019-05-28}}</ref> He has received the Gaetano Salvatore Gold Medal from Italy (2004). He was awarded the [[Kihara Memorial Foundation Academic Award]] in 1995 and the [[Medals of Honor (Japan)#Purple ribbon|Purple Ribbon Medal]] and the [[Medals of Honor (Japan)|Medal of Honor of Japan]] in 2009<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nig.ac.jp/nig/2009/11/research/prizes-and-awards/20091105.html|title=Prof. Takashi Gojobori was selected to receive the 2009 Autumn Purple Ribbon Medal|publisher=National Institute of Genetics|date=2009-11-05|access-date=2019-05-28}}</ref> for a series of his researches to pioneer the early age of "Molecular Evolutionary Studies using Genome Information." In 2022, he was elected as a [[ISCB Fellow|fellow]] of the [[International Society for Computational Biology]].<ref name="iscb-fellow">{{cite web |title=April 28, 2022: ISCB Congratulates and Introduces the 2022 Class of Fellows! |url=https://www.iscb.org/iscb-news-items/4861-april-28-2022-iscb-congratulates-and-introduces-the-2022-class-of-fellows |website=www.iscb.org |access-date=17 June 2022}}</ref>
